Text: went on a road trip with my best friend. We decided to rent a car because I could afford to buy gas. My friend picked up a map, drove us around for hours until we found a diner with a drive-thru window open.

We sat there drinking coffee and eating breakfast foods, watching the world go by.

I started thinking about what we would order if we were going somewhere else.

Finally, my turn arrived.

"What do you want?" asked my friend.

I looked down at my hands, feeling very nervous.

My friend took my hand and pulled me over to her window. She opened it wide enough for me to see outside.

There, sitting in the middle of the highway, were two guys holding hands.

One guy was tall, muscular, and wore a baseball cap. He smiled and said hi to us both.

The other guy was shorter than him, but equally as attractive. His eyes were bright blue, and his smile was warm and genuine.

"Hey," I said. "Do you mind if we join them? They seem really nice."

They turned around, and their smiles faded.

"No," said my friend. "Go ahead and sit next to them."

So I did. And they talked for a while. It wasn't awkward, though; it was natural. There was no sense of competition between us, and neither of them seemed rude.

Eventually, they left. We watched them drive away, our hearts racing.

"That was fun," I said.

My friend nodded. "Yeah, it was. But it doesn't mean anything anymore. You know why?"

"Because we won't ever forget that day," I replied.

She laughed. "Right! Because it's in your head forever."

And that's exactly right. That moment will always be etched into my memory. Even though it didn't lead anywhere significant, it was worth experiencing.
targets: went on a road trip with my best friend. We sat in a diner, watching two guys holding hands.

After leaving Bali, we tried to find out where the monkey came from. Turns out, there are lots of monkeys in Bali. Some are wild, others come from zoos.
